redFlags: Operator does NOT serve pembrokeshire, gower, anglesey, llyn-peninsula, or mid-wales — it is a single fixed-site mountain bike park at Mynydd Gethin, just outside Merthyr Tydfil, on the southern edge of Bannau Brycheiniog (Brecon Beacons) National Park. Combo pages referencing this operator in those five regions are a region mismatch and should be removed.
Correct regions are south-wales (Merthyr Tydfil / South Wales Valleys) and brecon-beacons (site sits on the park's southern boundary and is listed as a Brecon Beacons/Bannau Brycheiniog business).

Site's own contact page warns visitors not to navigate to its registered postcode (CF48 1YZ) as it leads to the wrong location — noted here so the address field isn't mistaken for a navigation-safe address.
No independently-sourced Google rating found (only TripAdvisor/Trustpilot review mentions); googleRating left null rather than guessed.
Precise lat/lng not confirmed from an authoritative source; left null pending a mapped confirmation rather than guessing coordinates.

proposedOperatorData.name: BikePark Wales
proposedOperatorData.tagline: The UK's leading gravity mountain bike park, on the southern edge of the Brecon Beacons
proposedOperatorData.description:
BikePark Wales is a purpose-built, uplift-served mountain bike park on Mynydd Gethin, just outside Merthyr Tydfil in the South Wales Valleys, on the southern edge of Bannau Brycheiniog (Brecon Beacons) National Park. The site holds over 40 trails across Blue, Red, Black and Pro grades on roughly 850 hectares, including Kermit, billed as the UK's longest beginner downhill trail, plus flow trails, technical black lines and big-air jump lines for advanced and expert riders.

On-site facilities include a paid uplift service, a bike shop and workshop, and a cafe. The park is oriented entirely around downhill and gravity mountain biking rather than general outdoor activities, and is not a walking, watersports or multi-activity centre.

Access is signposted from the M4 and A470; the operator's own site warns against navigating to its registered postcode as it does not lead to the correct entrance, so visitors should use the mapped directions on the BikePark Wales website.
